name: Safety
definition: The user can lose something without warning: a destructive action that runs without a confirmation or undo, or typed input that is lost when they leave. window.confirm dialogs and secret-shaped strings in client JS are already rule findings; do not repeat them. A static screen cannot show what a click does: ground a claim on the control (selector) and, when you read the handler in source, on file:line; answer cannot-judge when neither the evidence nor the source settles it.

checklist.question: Is there a destructive control (Delete, Remove, Reset, Discard, Cancel subscription, Clear all) with no sign of a confirmation step or undo: its accessible name and aria.yml show no dialog/menu popup, nothing on screen mentions undo or a trash, and (if you read it) its handler deletes immediately?

Is there a form or editor with several fields or free text where leaving controls (navigation links, Cancel, Close, Back) sit beside it with no sign of a draft, autosave or leave warning (no 'Saved', 'Draft', 'Unsaved changes' text)?

bad: A trash icon button named 'Delete garden' on each row; aria.yml shows a plain button, no popup, and the screen offers no undo.
A long 'New journal entry' editor with a 'Back' link and no 'Draft saved' indicator or leave warning.
good: 'Delete garden…' opens a dialog (aria-haspopup=dialog) that names the garden.
'Archive' moves a note to an Archive list the sidebar links to: it can be undone.
The editor shows 'Draft saved 2 min ago'.

severityRubric.blocker: a single click permanently deletes user data with no confirmation and no undo
severityRubric.high: a destructive action without confirmation on a core screen, or long input lost on leave
severityRubric.medium: a destructive action with no confirmation where the data can be recovered another way
severityRubric.low: short input (one field) lost on leave
